newsitem.title: USA: Orlando, Fla., airport eyes $965 million expansion.
newsitem.headline: Orlando, Fla., airport eyes $965 million expansion.

text.p: Florida's Orlando International Airport has proposed a $965 million expansion that would be financed mostly with revenue bonds, the Orlando Sentinel said Monday.

The plan calls for $432 million of revenue bonds backed by landing fees and airport rents and another $331 million backed by passenger facility charges. Most of the remaining money would come from federal grants.
The project would add parking, traffic and baggage handling facilities to the existing terminal that opened in 1981, and add a new south terminal.
The proposal must be approved by at least six of the airport's 11 signatory airlines, the major carriers who have oversight on debt financing that would affect their rents.

Bob Hattaway, chairman of the Greater Orlando Aviation Authority, said the expansion is needed to keep pace with spiraling passenger traffic at the fast-growing airport. He told the newspaper that he expects the carriers to approve it.
"We've worked very closely with the airlines on these issues and that's why I'm optimistic about our chances of getting their approval," Hattaway told the Sentinel.
